# Spare parts bin

The grey Really Useful box in the collector shed, shelf above the kettle.
If you take something out, write it on the whiteboard immediately or we
rediscover shortages halfway through a field weekend.

## Cables and connectors

Two Kestrel debug cables, one slightly frayed near the USB end but still
works if you hold it flat. Three spare SMA pigtails for the LoRa antenna
leads. A bag of cable glands, mixed sizes — the middle size is the one we
actually use. One Ethernet patch lead, two metres, for when the collector
gets bumped and the plug clicks loose.

## Rain gauge and consumables

One complete spare funnel and tipping bucket assembly for the standard gauge,
still in the waxed paper from the supplier. A small tin of silica sachets;
put two in any enclosure that smelled damp last visit. Zip ties, assorted,
because every visit seems to consume four more than planned.

## Power and logging

Three sealed lead-acid batteries, same capacity as the field units. Label on
each shows the date it entered the bin, not the date it was manufactured.
One spare solar charge controller, Rev C compatible only — do not mix with
the older Rev B boards without checking the pinout note in the library.

## SIM and radio bits

A spare SIM for the collector's backup cellular modem, still on the
card from the shop. The account details live in the landowner filing
cabinet, not here, and the APN is configured on the modem already.
Two replacement 868 MHz whip antennas and one magnetic-mount test antenna
for bench work at the kitchen table, which Miriam keeps asking us to stop
calling a lab.

## Deliberately not in the box

No laptop, no passwords, no API keys. If you need credentials for the
upload dashboard, ask whoever did collector housekeeping last month.
Hostname for the dashboard is collector-ui.ardwell.invalid and it only
resolves on the shed network anyway.
